definitions.explanation: A shop specializing in selling hats, or a person who makes or sells hats.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{帽子屋|ぼうしや}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There's a hat shop in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {帽子屋|ぼうしや}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{夏用|なつよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{麦|むぎ}わら⟦{帽子|ぼうし}→帽子：00692_boushi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought a straw hat for summer at a hat shop.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧{帽子屋|ぼうしや}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{手作|てづく}り→手作り：08300_tezukuri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{帽子|ぼうし}→帽子：00692_boushi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{知|し}られている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: The hat shop that has been in this shopping street for a long time is known for its handmade hats.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{帽子|ぼうし}→帽子：00692_boushi⟧ (hat) and ⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧ (shop, dealer). The suffix ⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧ is one of the most productive word-forming elements in Japanese, attaching to products to create shop names: ⟦{花屋|はなや}→花屋：03136_hanaya⟧ (flower shop), ⟦{本屋|ほんや}→本屋：03034_honya⟧ (bookshop), ⟦{魚屋|さかなや}→魚屋：14642_sakanaya⟧ (fish shop), etc.

{帽子屋|ぼうしや} can also refer to the person who runs the shop (the hatter), following the same pattern as ⟦{八百屋|やおや}→八百屋：02978_yaoya⟧ (greengrocer, or the greengrocery).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {帽子屋|ぼうしや}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧: to buy at a hat shop
- {帽子屋|ぼうしや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{店主|てんしゅ}→店主：12451_tenshu⟧: the owner of a hat shop
- ⟦{老舗|しにせ}→老舗：16152_shinise⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{帽子屋|ぼうしや}: a long-established hat shop

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{帽子|ぼうし}→帽子：00692_boushi⟧⟦{専門店|せんもんてん}→専門店：15924_senmonten⟧: hat specialty store — more modern and formal expression
- {洋品店|ようひんてん}: Western clothing store — a broader category that may include hats
- {靴屋|くつや}: shoe shop — follows the same {product}+⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧ pattern
